channel.title: The Runesmith Devlog
channel.description: Development log of The Runesmith, a crafting RPG about a fallen god forging runes to climb back home. What we built, what we cut, and what comes next.

item.title: A new look for the interface
item.description: The gothic frames are gone. The HUD, health bars, inventory, tooltips and equipment panel all moved to a new, calmer style I've been calling Night Sky, built to a design mockup down to the pixel.

item.title: Hits, dodges and menus that answer back
item.description: A stat you can't see working might as well not exist. This round gave dodges, blocks and bonus loot their own feedback, put motion into every menu, and fixed a camera that kept jumping at you.

item.title: Runes that keep their promises
item.description: Thirty-four rune stats used to show up on your runes and then do nothing at all. This week every one of them got wired into the game, and Shatter, the strangest of them, got a look of its own.

item.title: Getting ready for Next Fest
item.description: The demo is heading to Steam Next Fest, October 19 to 26. This update is all about the first hour and the last minute of it: hits that land harder, forging that reveals its rarity, a starter rune you get to pick, and a proper goodbye when the demo ends.

item.title: The Runesmith now speaks 33 languages
item.description: The whole game is now translated into 33 languages, from Japanese to Ukrainian. Also in this update: a fix for the freeze when a big hit drops a mountain of loot, crafted gear you can finally pull out of a bench, and better tools for testing.

item.title: 66 achievements and a better pickup
item.description: The Runesmith now has 66 Steam achievements, each with its own hand-made icon and an in-game panel to track them. Picking things off the ground got an animation, and combat got a combo counter.

item.title: Giving the forge a voice
item.description: Two days rebuilding how The Runesmith sounds. Every sound now comes from one place, the main menu finally makes noise, and every button in the game clicks. Cutscenes also stopped letting you open your inventory mid-scene.

item.title: Settings, safety nets and a sky that behaves
item.description: A real pause menu and settings screen, a no-penalty rescue for when you fall off the world, hits you can actually feel, and a day-night cycle that stays in its best hours.

item.title: The gods wake up
item.description: The six god statues now shatter and reassemble in their reveal, the first boss gets a proper entrance, and every bench can finally reach into your chests. Plus a long, quiet optimization pass.
